Formulation:
- Concise formulation: Acute respiratory viral illness (most likely viral URTI/acute bronchitis) presenting with 5–6 days of continuous dry cough, rhinorrhea, nocturnal cough disrupting sleep, subjective fever/chills, myalgias and marked fatigue leading to functional impairment (lying in bed, missed work day). Contributing factors include underlying medical comorbidities (type 2 diabetes, hypertension) which may increase risk of complications. Differential considerations include influenza, COVID-19 (both medium likelihood per DDx) and ACE inhibitor–induced cough as an alternative or contributing factor. Psychosocial perpetuating factors: return to work despite illness and ongoing cough causing sleep disruption and frustration. Protective factors: partner support, access to GP care, patient willingness to rest and follow advice.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis (probable)
- Patient Goal(s): Symptomatic recovery; reduced cough frequency, improved sleep and energy; return to usual work activities
- Clinical Goal(s): Symptomatic relief; monitor for clinical deterioration; identify alternative causes if cough persists beyond expected course
- Actions (Patient):
  - Rest and conserve energy; limit work for 1–2 days if possible
  - Maintain hydration; use regular paracetamol for fever/aches as needed
  - Reduce alcohol consumption as advised (doctor suggested cutting down)
  - Return for review if no improvement in 2–3 days or sooner if breathing worsens, fever persists, or new severe symptoms occur
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide symptomatic care advice (rest, fluids, paracetamol)
  - Monitor course with plan to reassess in 2–3 days if not improving; earlier review if worsening respiratory symptoms
  - Consider diagnostic testing (e.g., COVID-19 or influenza testing) if clinically indicated or if symptoms persist/worsen
  - Consider antibiotic therapy only if clinical features suggest bacterial chest infection (fever persists, focal chest signs) per clinician plan
  - If cough persists beyond expected timeframe, review for alternative causes including ACE inhibitor–related cough and consider medication review/adjustment in liaison with prescribing clinician

Secondary Problem: Influenza (possible)
- Patient Goal(s): Symptomatic resolution and prevention of complications
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify if influenza is the cause when clinically appropriate; provide supportive care; consider antiviral therapy if within treatment window and indicated
- Actions (Patient):
  - As above (rest, fluids, seek testing if advised)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Assess for influenza testing or antiviral eligibility if presentation or public health guidance indicates
  - Continue symptomatic management and safety-netting advice

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Rest, hydration, symptomatic measures (paracetamol), recommendation to reduce alcohol intake, advice to take 1–2 days off work if possible, and instructions to return earlier if breathing worsens or fever persists
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing breathlessness, persistent or high fever, worsening chest pain, hemoptysis, marked functional decline
- Coping Strategies: Rest, hydration, use of paracetamol for fever/aches, temporary reduction in work duties/hours, reduce alcohol intake

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal consent recorded in dialogue)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Patient to return if no improvement within 2–3 days or sooner if breathing worsens or new severe symptoms occur

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- No mental health differential diagnoses supported by the transcript or DDx. The DDx provided relates to respiratory/infectious and medication-related causes (viral URTI/acute bronchitis — High; Influenza — Medium; ACE inhibitor–induced cough — Medium; COVID-19 — Medium).

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Formal mental health history and prior psychiatric diagnoses not recorded
  - Formal Mental Status Examination details (orientation, cognition, formal mood/affect rating) are not recorded
  - Suicidality/self-harm risk level not documented
  - No objective vital signs or examination findings recorded (temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, chest auscultation)
  - No documentation of COVID-19/influenza testing status
  - No documentation of medication doses/frequencies for listed medications

● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified between transcript and DDx; both align that a viral respiratory illness is most likely. (Conflict between ACE inhibitor cough vs infectious etiology noted in DDx reasoning — both listed as considerations.)

● Transcript quality notes:
  - Transcript appears to capture a near-complete consultation focused on acute physical illness; audio/dialogue intermittently contains pauses and brief overlapping speech but key information is present.
  - No formal psychiatrically focused questions were asked; mental health-specific information is limited.
